target_offset_note:
[0.02, -0.0293, 0.025] SINCE 2026-09-11, walked out on the floor-5 hall call button of the new building.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and why this one is better evidence than the guesses before it: the robot drove to f5_call_button, pressed on its own, and the operator then moved the arm BY HAND to where it actually touches the button. The arm's own encoders recorded the move: dx 0.0, dy -31.3, dz 0.0 mm. That is a direct measurement of the residual in the arm's own frame, not a number inferred from a miss. A further +7 mm of x was added at the operator's request, then the press was re-run from stow and the arm walked forward in 8/8/5 mm steps until the operator confirmed it was pressing: +21 mm more x. Total x offset was 0.028; the next autonomous run hit the panel but pressed slightly into the wall, so 8 mm came back off -> 0.020. The confirming pose has flange x 659.8 mm, which is the SAME x the arm was at during the earlier hand-set contact -- two independent confirmations agreeing to a millimetre.

THE SIGN, AGAIN. +y in link_base is the ROBOT's left, the OPERATOR's right when facing it. The correction here is -y, i.e. toward the operator's left.

WHAT IS STILL UNRESOLVED. This offset makes the press land, but it does not explain WHY the raw aim was out. The reach is accurate to 2-6 mm across the plate and only wrong along the approach axis, and both the camera and the lidar agree the front of the arm assembly sits within about 30 mm of the flange face -- which is incompatible with the 172 mm tool_tip_mm the code assumes. Until the real flange-to-fingertip distance is measured, this offset is a working correction at ~0.7 m and should not be trusted at a different range.

CONTACT EVIDENCE EXISTS AFTER ALL. This note previously said collision_sensitivity reads 0 so contact cannot raise error 31 and 'the move completed' is the only signal. That is FALSE, demonstrated 2026-09-11 on the floor-1 ADA plate: the reach tripped ControllerError 31 at flange x 591.9 and the operator confirmed it as contact in the right place -- the first press all session with evidence rather than inference. bringup/mission.sh already relied on this ('CONTACT IS THE PRESS SUCCEEDING ... only 31: 21/22/23/24 mean the arm never got there'); this file was the thing that was wrong. Treat 31 on a reach as contact, and its ABSENCE as the thing that proves nothing.
tool_tip_note:
172 mm, the catalogue figure for an xArm Gripper, STILL UNVERIFIED on this build -- see docs/CALIBRATION.md item 2.

A 392 mm value was written here on 2026-09-11 and REVERTED the same hour. It came from driving the arm until the operator confirmed physical contact with the floor-5 call button and reading the encoders: the modelled 172 mm tip sat 220 mm PAST the grounded button, 24 mm off across. I read that as 'the tool is 220 mm longer than modelled' and stored 172+220.

That was wrong, and the geometry says so: with 392 mm the modelled tip starts 194 mm PAST the button at the ready pose, so a press would require the arm to move BACKWARDS. Run the other way, the same measurement means the point that actually touched is ~48 mm BEHIND the flange face -- which is the wrist housing, not a fingertip. The photo taken at that pose agrees: the white wrist is against the plate with nothing projecting past it.

So the measurement was of the WRIST touching, not the tool, and it cannot calibrate a tool tip. What is physically on the flange, and how far it projects, is still unanswered and is the thing blocking presses on this rig.
notes: 2026-09-11 f5 call button, two-move approach (align 45 mm, then push to -200 mm): operator confirmed the press twice ('PERFECT', 'PERFECT AGAIN'), asking only for ~1 mm more forward. x offset 0.020 -> 0.021 m. This is a ~1 mm trim on a working press, not a re-derivation -- the underlying tool length (172 mm) is still unverified.
target_offset_profiles_note:
lift_car_select = [0.027, -0.0443, 0.025] SINCE 2026-09-11. THE ELEVATOR CAR PANEL, which is a
DIFFERENT calibration from the hall call plate and must stay that way -- the call plate uses the
default target_offset_link_base_m and the operator asked explicitly that the two not be merged.
Select it with --offset-profile lift_car_select or UTP_OFFSET_PROFILE=lift_car_select.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED. Floor 5, robot inside the car, pressing the floor-1 button. Started from the
call-plate default, which the operator called 'VERY close'; then -20 y, +3 x, (+5 y, +2 x), +1 x,
each applied between presses with the operator looking at the contact. Final press confirmed HIT.

HOW MUCH TO TRUST EACH STEP. Only the LAST step is clean. The first three corrections were measured
while the wrist was sitting in a MIRRORED IK BRANCH: joints read J4 -180.5 / J6 +180.7, two ~180
degree rolls that nearly cancel, so the tool still pointed at the plate and the presses still landed,
but the arm was not in the configuration the IK had planned. The tool tip is 172 mm past the flange,
so a few degrees of wrist difference moves the tip ~10 mm -- larger than the 5 mm corrections being
applied. Some of those early corrections were therefore absorbing configuration, not calibration.
The final press was re-run from an exact-joint ready pose, came back to rpy [164.9, -87.3, 15.4]
(identical to the first press of the session) with no flip, and was confirmed by the operator.

WHY THE WRIST WAS FLIPPING. approach_target.py --hold re-saves calib/arm_home.json from the arm's
ACTUAL start pose each run, and --retreat-only commands that pose back in CARTESIAN space, which
does not pin the IK branch. Cycle after cycle the returned pose drifted (roll 164.9 -> 161.8 ->
157.6, yaw 15.4 -> 19.5 -> 22.9) until the solver settled in the mirrored branch. RESET BETWEEN
PRESSES WITH JOINT ANGLES, i.e. stow_arm.py --ready, which commands exact joint targets and is
repeatable. A Cartesian retreat alone is not a reset.

REPRODUCING THIS PRESS. Arm at ready (stow_arm.py --ready --go), then:
  UTP_REACH_MARGIN_M=0.03 python3 bringup/approach_target.py --capture <capture> --go \
      --min-standoff -200 --speed 80 --hold --offset-profile lift_car_select
Confirmed press: flange [643.1, -0.9, 317.4] rpy [164.9, -87.3, 15.4], joints
[-0.7, 19.1, -47.5, -1.3, -59.0, -0.9], target in link_base [0.610, -0.0132, 0.3282], 0.693 m out.

GROUNDING ON THIS PANEL IS NOT RELIABLE. Two groundings of the same query seconds apart, arm and
base unmoved, returned bbox [659,693,690,718] (camera y +0.340) and bbox [616,135,645,165]
(camera y -0.232) -- about 570 mm apart vertically, different buttons. The second was vetoed by
check_press_safe.py as 'a red emergency call button' (95% overlap, 2 of 4 forbidden queries). The
press above was run against a capture the operator had confirmed by eye AND which passed the veto
clean. DO NOT let this profile imply the detector can pick the floor button unsupervised here.

THE CAVEATS ON THE DEFAULT OFFSET APPLY HERE TOO: tool_tip_mm 172 is unverified, and
collision_sensitivity reads 0, so 'the move completed' remains the only contact signal.
